greeting.speaker: MCCLAWSKY
greeting.text: Let's go, big man. The meter's running, and I've got a wife who thinks I'm at a prayer group.

opening.speaker: SAL
opening.text: The Sasquatches are making business difficult.

opening.speaker: PROSPECT
opening.text: You put four in my uncle outside a fruit stand six years ago and now you want to talk about routes.

opening.speaker: PROSPECT
opening.text: You shot Booski. In the stomach. Four times. Six years ago. He healed mean and still sends you a card every anniversary, so.

opening.speaker: MCCLAWSKY
opening.text: Your people ought to settle down some. I'm saying that as a friend, more or less. It's not a threat. But it's not not a threat, either.

opening.speaker: PROSPECT
opening.text: You broke my jaw outside a hospital and then filed it as resisting. I've read the report. It's beautiful. You should write books.

opening.speaker: SAL
opening.text: I want the servers, the skin market, and Wednesday nights.

opening.speaker: SAL
opening.text: Belongs. That's a beautiful word. My father used it about a farm in Calabria that has had six owners since he said it. Things don't belong to people. Things sit with people, for a while, until somebody with more men wants them to sit somewhere else.

opening.speaker: SAL
opening.text: Help me, kid. Your family keeps the name, keeps the corners, keeps the funerals small. I take a slice off the top and nobody has to bury anybody they like.

opening.speaker: PROSPECT
opening.text: How big a slice are we calling a percentage?

opening.stage: Prospect looks toward the bathroom hallway.

excuse.stage: McClawsky looks at Sal. Sal gives a small nod.

final.speaker: SAL
final.text: So. Do we have an understanding, or do I finish my drink and make some calls?

final.speaker: SAL
final.text: Good. The Sasquatches keep their name.

final.stage: The train grows louder. The glasses begin to vibrate.

final.speaker: SAL
final.text: Tell your people the business is settled.

extraction.speaker: DRIVER
extraction.text: Lou says you're sleeping up north tonight. Get in.
